note: M20 icons v2 — production slice A02. Style is D22/R1 "True colour": the icon IS the official mark, fitted, official colours verbatim. Per L2 every mark's geometry derives from official vector artwork; this file records where each one came from, exactly what L5 forced us to simplify, and every judgement call made along the way. The set constants were ruled with the pilot and are referenced, not re-decided.

slice.label: A02 — the code category, bosque to falcon, the second 84 concepts of the long tail
slice.modules_note: the slice is built by three tranches in parallel; a missing module means that share of the roster is not built yet, which is reported and is only fatal once all three are present

tooling.fetched artwork: m20-icons-v2/sources-svg/ — brand-published SVGs, downloaded once and kept for the standing fidelity gate
tooling.engine: tools/spec-engine.mjs — the pilot's fit machinery, shared verbatim

set_constants.typeset_letters: NONE. R1 has no typeset letters; the L3 table stays dormant. Any letterform in this slice is faithful source geometry from a brand's own artwork.

families.rule: WORKING RULE 1 (opened with this slice). A concept that is a variant of a branded family adapts the source themes' established NON-LETTER variant glyph in the family's official colours where one exists (branch a); where the variant differs only by letters or has no distinct variant glyph, it ships the family base mark IDENTICALLY under its own id (branch b). Byte-identity inside a declared family is expected: the twin audit reports those pairs in a family lane instead of failing them, and never exempts them silently.

al.why: Microsoft ships ONE AL mark for this language family and registers it against the `al` language id, so every variant takes it byte-identically. `dal` (this tranche): the roster gives it the extension .dal AND the language id `dal` while A01's `al-dal` has the extension .dal, so the two concepts claim the same file type — the asp/aspx situation — and vscode-icons' own icon requests say what it is (#1159 asks for the AL icon "via language id `al`, `dal`"; #3125 calls .dal "AL Language definition files"). Branch (a) is empty twice over: the theme's file_type_dal.svg is a bar chart with a rising arrow and its file_type_al_dal.svg is the AL monogram recoloured dusty red, which A01 already declined. `c-al` (tranche 1): C/AL is AL's direct ancestor in the same product line, and branch (a) there is the Microsoft Dynamics 365 sail — a product-suite mark rather than a C/AL variant glyph. Tranche 1's own entry carries that reasoning in full

sap.why: .cds is a Core Data Services model in SAP's Cloud Application Programming model, so SAP's mark applies for the same reason it applies to abap (the company-mark rider, ratified at the A01 gate). No source theme draws a distinct non-letter CDS glyph — Material draws a cloud with an arrow, a platform metaphor — so branch (b) applies

coldfusion.why: RULED 2026-09-03 — Sebastian, overturning flag 1: "In those cases you can use a background in a frame with their corners rounded (like in previous iterations)", and, on which frame, "Adobe's own framed icon — fetch Adobe's actual ColdFusion product icon: bright rounded frame + dark field + Cf letters, colors verbatim." So cf ships Adobe's framed ColdFusion construction and is the family base. Adobe publishes ONE ColdFusion mark, not one per file extension, and no source theme draws a distinct non-letter variant glyph for a .cfc or a .cfm — vscode-icons redraws the same Cf plate for both — so branch (a) has nothing to adapt and cfc and cfm ship the base byte-identically under their own ids

chef.why: a .ckbk is a Chef cookbook, the same family one level down. vscode-icons composes a BOOK with the chef mark on its cover, which is its own composition rather than a variant glyph, so branch (a) has nothing to adapt and the variant ships the family base mark byte-identically

dotnet.why: a .csproj is an MSBuild project file for a .NET project, so the .NET mark applies for the same reason it applies to A01's asp and aspx, which its fix round already ruled one family on Microsoft's CC0 .NET logo. Branch (a) was checked and declined: vscode-icons draws the Visual Studio ribbon with a green "C#" over it, which is the IDE's corporate mark composed with a language monogram rather than a .NET variant glyph. So csproj ships the family base byte-identically

latex.why: .dtx is the literate LaTeX source the `doctex` language id names (the roster carries both because Material registers the extension and the language separately — the asp/aspx situation A01 ruled on) and .ins is the docstrip installer that unpacks it. One brand, one file family, and the LaTeX Project's own kingfisher is the mark all three wear under the company-mark rider. Branch (a) is empty: no source theme draws a distinct non-letter variant glyph for either variant — Material registers both ids against its own "TEX" logotype in blue, a monogram it set rather than anything the brand draws

neutral_collapse.rule: WORKING RULE 2 (opened with this slice). After a genuine hunt proves no usable mark, a concept takes a neutral vocabulary glyph in the shared gray: the object it names where there is one, otherwise its CATEGORY glyph. Category glyphs are shared byte for byte across every concept that falls back to them; every collapsed subject is listed here and reported in the twin audit's neutral lane.

fix_round.verdict: Sebastian at the A02 gate, on the seven asks the slice presented: "Approved." Six went through as built — c-al and dal on Microsoft's AL mark, buckbuild's antler monogram over Buck 2's deer, cuda wearing NVIDIA's eye, the duckdb look-alike pairs, and the smaller calls on dune, ejs, eex/erb and elm. The LaTeX kingfisher was queried, explained and then confirmed AS BUILT. One was OVERTURNED, with a directive rather than a preference: cf / cfc / cfm, flag 1 — "In those cases you can use a background in a frame with their corners rounded (like in previous iterations)" — and, asked which frame, "Adobe's own framed icon — fetch Adobe's actual ColdFusion product icon: bright rounded frame + dark field + Cf letters, colors verbatim."
fix_round.binding: THE FRAMED-CONSTRUCTION LAW. A mark whose own FIELD cannot clear the backdrop may ship the brand's own FRAMED construction: the frame carries the silhouette against #121314, and the dark field inside it is then MARK-INTERIOR INK, which is never lifted — the same reading the §5 lift/plate erratum already makes for dotenv's black on its own yellow field. So a dark plate is no longer "lift it or drop it"; the question is whether the brand draws a frame. The frame must BE the brand's, derived from the brand's own artwork like any other geometry (L2 is untouched), and it still has to clear L5 at 16 px. Guide-erratum grade: the session folds it into §5.
fix_round.unchanged: Everything else A02 was gated on. The D22 licence amendment and the company-mark rider carried from A01 are unchanged and were not re-argued; L2's ban on tracing a raster or drawing freehand still binds, which is why the ColdFusion letters ship at Adobe's own weight instead of being thickened; L5's physics, true colour, the ban on typeset letters, the twin audit, the family / collapse / look-alike lanes and the neutral vocabulary all stand. Provenance duty is untouched: both Adobe cuts and the two sibling icons the frame geometry was measured on are fetched, kept in sources-svg/ and recorded verbatim.
fix_round.scale: 3 of 84 rebuilt — the ColdFusion trio, cf / cfc / cfm, which is one payload under three ids. The kingfisher trio (latex, ltx, sty) was queried and CONFIRMED AS BUILT, not rebuilt. The other 81 subjects are byte-identical to the gated build.
fix_round.flags: the gate's flags keep the numbers 1-51 it was decided on; flag 1 is marked SUPERSEDED in place with a pointer, because deleting it would delete the measurement that produced the ruling. The round's own flags are 52 and 53.

notes.cf: flag 1 declined Adobe's ColdFusion plate on a measurement — a #002258 field at 1.21:1 against #121314 — and the ruling overturns it by supplying a construction: the brand's own FRAMED icon, where the frame carries the silhouette and the dark field becomes mark-interior ink. Adobe publishes that frame (adobe.com/content/dam/shared/images/product-icons/svg/coldfusion.svg, internally cf_builder_2016_appicon.svg) as a ring inset 10.7 on a 256-wide icon; FrameMaker and RoboHelp, served beside it, are 10/240 = w/24 exactly. Adobe's framed cut is square-cornered, so the ruling's rounded corners come from Adobe's own rounded framed cut (photoshop-ipad-official.svg), whose outer radius IS ColdFusion's plate radius to five decimals and whose inner radius is 0.8541 of it. One number moved: w/24 is 0.53 px at the shipped fit, so the prettier rider thickens the frame to w/10 = 1.28 px, the smallest denominator that clears L5's 1.2 px floor (w/11 = 1.16 px was measured and rejected).
notes.cfc: rule 1(b) of the rebuilt cf, byte for byte: Adobe publishes one ColdFusion mark and no source theme draws a distinct .cfc variant glyph. The family key changed with the construction — `adobe` (pointing at A01's actionscript) is gone and `coldfusion` has cf as its own base.
notes.cfm: rule 1(b) of the rebuilt cf, byte for byte, for the same reason as cfc.

lookalike.rule: DECLARED LOOK-ALIKE PAIRS, opened by the fix round. Two brands whose REAL marks genuinely resemble each other may both keep them: the pair is declared here, reported by the twin audit with its live R7/R8 scores on every run, and never failed. An UNDECLARED pair scoring the same still fails, and the lane prints exactly what it is exempting — it is a lane, not a mute button.

Neither brand offers a non-round cut: the design manual's other DuckDB cuts are the same head in a lockup, and the Emacs icon is a sphere in every size the tree ships. Form 0.986 on the 0.72 silhouette bar, the highest in the slice

flags.title: cf / cfc / cfm — Adobe publishes a ColdFusion mark and this build declines it
flags.superseded: OVERTURNED by the A02 gate ruling (2026-09-03). Sebastian: "In those cases you can use a background in a frame with their corners rounded (like in previous iterations)" — and, on which frame, "Adobe's own framed icon". The 1.21:1 measurement below still stands and is still the reason the BARE plate could not ship; what the ruling changed is that a field which cannot clear the backdrop no longer ends the hunt, because the brand's own FRAMED construction puts a silhouette around it. All three now ship Adobe's framed ColdFusion icon; see flag 52. Kept in place because the hunt and the measurement it records are still the hunt and the measurement.
flags.text: The flag to argue with if any of them is. .cfm and .cfc are Adobe ColdFusion files, and unlike A01's actionscript — which never had a mark of its own — ColdFusion HAS one: the 2021 product icon, a #002258 rounded square carrying a pale-blue "Cf". It is fetched, built and rendered in proofs/A02-t1-study.png, and it is declined on a MEASUREMENT rather than on the A01 reading that a letter plate is a monogram in a box. The number: that navy field measures 1.21:1 against #121314 — below even bicep's 2.04:1, which the pilot rejected — so on the product backdrop the plate is not there. What arrives at 16 px is two pale-blue letters floating in space, which is exactly the typeset-letter icon R1 abolished, and lifting the field to clear the bar would invent a colour Adobe does not print. So all three ship Adobe's corporate red A, byte-identical to A01's actionscript and adobe-swc. What that costs in the tree: five ids — .as, .swc, .cfm, .cfc, .cfml — now look the same. That is rule 1(b) working as written, and the alternative is a plate you cannot see. To overturn: say the Cf plate ships and it does, with its field lifted or with the letters alone.

flags.title: c-al takes Microsoft's AL mark, not the Dynamics 365 sail
flags.text: A .cal is a C/AL source file — Client/server Application Language, the language of Dynamics NAV and the direct ancestor of AL, which A01 already ships with Microsoft's own #2EA98E lockup. Rule 1 asks branch (a) first, and there IS an established variant glyph here: vscode-icons draws the Microsoft Dynamics 365 sail for c-al. It is declined because that sail is the mark of the whole product suite — Sales, Finance, Supply Chain, Business Central and the rest — rather than anything to do with C/AL; using it puts a corporate suite mark on a language file, one step further out than the company-mark rider reaches, and it would also be the only Dynamics-marked icon in the set. Microsoft itself ships ONE mark for this language family and registers it against the al language id. So branch (b): c-al is byte-identical to slices/A01/masters/al.svg, and the slice check asserts that rather than trusting it. In the tree an .al and a .cal will look the same. To overturn: rule that the Dynamics sail may stand for C/AL and it becomes a one-source hunt.

flags.title: cds wears SAP's mark — the company-mark rider, used for the second time
flags.text: A .cds is a Core Data Services model in SAP's Cloud Application Programming model, and the language ids the roster records (cds, cds-markdown-injection) are the SAP CDS extension's. The company-mark rider ratified at the A01 gate — a format created and owned by a company may wear that company's mark — therefore fires exactly as it did for abap, and cds ships the SAP parallelogram byte-identically. Worth knowing before you agree: this is the second SAP-marked icon in the set, so an .abap and a .cds are now the same picture, and CDS is a little further from SAP than ABAP is — ABAP exists nowhere but inside a SAP system, while .cds files are written by anyone using the (Apache-2.0, npm-published) CAP toolchain. It is still SAP's language and SAP's specification. Material's alternative is a cloud with an arrow through it, which is a metaphor for "cloud platform" and not a mark.

flags.title: chef — Chef's own arc mark, not the Progress corporate symbol chef.io serves
flags.text: The hunt turned up two marks and they are not the same brand. What chef.io serves today is progress-chef-primary-logo-svg.svg: the PROGRESS corporate symbol — Progress acquired Chef in 2020 — beside a "Progress Chef" wordmark. What ships is Chef's own arc "C", the concentric orange-and-slate ring the project used through 2020, which gilbarbara/logos carries as a vector in both official colours and which simple-icons, vscode-icons and Material all still draw. The reasoning is the mirror image of the cds flag: putting the PARENT COMPANY's symbol on a Berksfile would be a corporate mark standing in for a product that has its own, where the rider only covers a company standing in for a format it owns. The honest caveat: Chef's arc mark is retired branding. If you would rather the set follow the current owner, the Progress symbol is one fetch away.

flags.title: chef — thirteen arc segments, and why none of them is deleted
flags.text: Chef's mark is a "C" built from thirteen concentric arc segments, which is far past L5's "about three distinguishable sub-shapes". It ships whole anyway, and here is the working. They are not thirteen sub-shapes: they are ONE ring, and at the compact envelope the segments span 1.54×2.58 px at the smallest and 10.88×5.60 at the largest, with the mark's sustained ink runs at 0.53 px at the 5th percentile, 1.09 at the 25th and 1.22 at the median — three times jar's 0.38, which A01 rejected, and still under the 1.2 px official-forced floor at the quartile. Every reduction that would buy thicker ink deletes rings, and a Chef mark with its rings deleted is a plain letter C, which is the gestalt failure the pilot ruling names (docker's deck, editorconfig's linework). The 16 px verdict is marginal and says so: what arrives is an orange-and-slate target, not a legible set of concentric arcs. Colour: the #435363 slate measures 2.35:1 against #121314 — under the 3.0:1 lift trigger — and is deliberately NOT lifted: it is the second tone of a two-tone mark whose primary is #F38B00 at 7.53:1, and lifting it to L 88 (#DBE0E6) would make Chef's slate the palest thing in the icon.

flags.title: bucklescript ships ReScript's mark — a SUCCESSOR-BRAND call, not a company one
flags.text: A new shape of call, so it is flagged rather than assumed. bsconfig.json, .bsb.lock and .cmj are BuckleScript's file names, and BuckleScript no longer exists as a brand: it renamed itself ReScript in August 2020 — the same repository, now rescript-lang/rescript-compiler — and bucklescript.github.io today serves one meta-refresh to rescript-lang.org and nothing else. bsconfig.json stayed ReScript's own config file name until v11 renamed it. The hunt: BuckleScript's own mark could not be found at all — the redirect leaves nothing behind, BuckleScript/bucklescript.github.io keeps no branding directory, and neither simple-icons nor gilbarbara/logos has ever carried a bucklescript entry. Material draws a teal "BS" plate, which is its own monogram. So the successor's own brand file ships, which is a RENAME rather than a company standing in for a format — closer to al/al-dal than to safetensors. One consequence to note: when a later slice reaches rescript, the two ids will want the same mark and will have to be declared a family across slices.

flags.title: cabal ships a five-pointed star, which is the whole of Cabal's symbol
flags.text: Not a legibility flag — an IDENTITY one. haskell/cabal-website publishes images/Cabal.svg, and the mark in it is one star plus the "Cabal" logotype; drop the logotype, as every icon in this set does, and what is left is a plain five-pointed star. It reads perfectly at 16 px (9.42×12.40 px of ink, runs 1.81 px at the 25th percentile and 5.47 at the median) and it is the most generic shape any subject in this tranche ships — nothing about it says Haskell, or build tool, or Cabal. It is nonetheless the brand's own symbol, and inventing something more distinctive is exactly what L2 forbids. Colour: the file carries the lockup twice, once for light grounds and once for dark; the dark-ground copy's star is #567DD9 (4.72:1) and the light-ground copy's is #2E5BC1, which measures 3.00:1 and still trips the lift by a hair, so the dark-ground copy ships. The alternative is Haskell's own lambda for Cabal's files, which would be a language's mark on its build tool — the cds rider stretched further than it has been stretched so far.

flags.title: buckbuild — the brand tier was sourced and then declined on L5
flags.text: The only subject in this tranche where the fidelity chain and the physics disagree, so it is written out in full. .buckconfig, .buckjavaargs and BUCK are read by BOTH generations of Meta's build system, and the two generations draw different marks. Buck 2 (facebook/buck2, current) publishes a real vector at website/static/img/logo.svg: a leaping deer in an #AF4F39 → #F69635 gradient. Buck 1 (facebook/buck, archived) draws an antler monogram and publishes it as docs/static/logo.png, a 300×150 raster that vscode-icons and Material both trace. The chain says Buck 2 and L5 overrules it, measured at a true 16 px rather than argued: the deer's sustained ink runs are 0.22 px at the 5th percentile, 0.38 at the 25th and 0.88 at the median — jar's numbers, which A01 rejected on L5 alone — and opening its envelope to 13.6×14.4 moves them only to 0.25 / 0.41 / 0.94. At 16 px it is an orange hook with a fork on top. The antler monogram runs 0.50 / 0.97 / 1.25 px at the same three percentiles and every tine survives, because its strokes are axis-aligned or at 45° and land on pixel edges. The honest limit: 1.25 px at the median is still under L5's 1.5 px floor — this is the better of two sub-floor marks, not a comfortable one. All three renders are in proofs/A02-t1-study.png. What this costs, and it is the reason to flag it: the set now carries the RETIRED generation's mark for a file the current one also reads. To overturn: rule that the current brand's vector ships whatever it looks like at 16 px, and the deer goes back in one edit.

flags.title: bruno drops the black keyline that Bruno's dog is drawn with
flags.text: Bruno's mark is a golden retriever's head drawn with a heavy black keyline, and the keyline is dropped. Two reasons, both measured. Bytes: it is the biggest path in the source — 3037 characters of 6.5 KB — and keeping it puts the icon over L8's 4 KB hard cap, which is a fail and not an advisory. Contrast: it measures 1.13:1 against #121314, so on the product backdrop it paints nothing a reader can see; the safetensors precedent (finger seams, same two reasons at once) is the shape of this call. What it costs is that the head keeps its full outer contour instead of being trimmed by an invisible line, which makes the dog very slightly larger than the official drawing. The eyes, the nose and the muzzle line stay black — they print on the mark's own golden field, where the pilot's dotenv erratum says ink is never lifted, and they are what makes the shape a dog. Sourcing note: usebruno/bruno publishes PNG only and simple-icons' bruno is a monochrome OUTLINE, so the geometry is vscode-icons' full-colour vector — R1 keeps multi-colour marks multi-colour.

flags.title: cakephp's cream bands are negative space, so they read dark
flags.text: CakePHP's mark is a three-tier cake, and the cream between the tiers is not ink: in every official version — the red one on a white page and the white one on cakephp.org's dark pages alike — the bands are the ground showing through. So they stay negative space here and read dark, and the cake arrives at 16 px as three red tiers rather than as red-and-cream. This is NOT the gpg move: there the official logo genuinely prints the GNU's mane white over the blue lock, so there was white ink to restore. What the alternative looks like: vscode-icons paints the bands white explicitly, which is a prettier icon at this size and is not the mark; both are side by side in proofs/A02-t1-study.png. Sourcing: the fetched file is CakePHP's WHITE lockup (the one it uses on dark pages); the three cake layers ship in the brand's published red #D33C43, which is the npm/git/go colour rule.

flags.title: cairo is Starknet's language, not the graphics library — and its runner is a hole
flags.text: Two things worth checking. Which Cairo: the roster's .cairo / languageId cairo is StarkWare's provable-computation language, not the cairo graphics library — simple-icons' cairographics is the library's mark and using it here would put the wrong project's logo on the file type. Starknet publishes the Cairo mark as raster everywhere (cairo-logo-square.png, Cairo_logo_500x500.png, PNG favicons on cairo-lang.org), so the geometry is vscode-icons' vector of it. The runner: the mark is one red contour with the running figure cut OUT of the disc and open to the outside at the lower left. There is no white ink in it — the runner is white on a white page because the page is white — and there is no closed contour to repaint, so on #121314 the figure reads dark. That is what the mark does on any dark ground, including Starknet's own dark lockups, but it does mean the icon arrives as a red disc with a dark bite rather than as a red disc with a white runner.

flags.title: caddy's ring is a three-stop gradient and neither end of it can ship
flags.text: A flattening decision that is not the chrome default, so here is the arithmetic. Caddy paints its ring with a three-stop linear gradient: rgb(35,217,59) green → rgb(119,196,247) pale blue → rgb(0,89,209) deep blue. L2's "dominant flat stop" is normally offset 1 (the chrome ruling), and here offset 1 measures 2.97:1 against #121314 — three hundredths under the 3.0:1 lift trigger, so taking it would immediately lift Caddy's blue to L 88 and repaint the mark pale. Offset 0 is the same green as the shed inside the ring, so taking it would flatten the whole symbol to one colour. What ships is #1F88C0, the flat Caddy blue simple-icons records for the brand: it sits inside the ramp and measures 4.73:1. brand-colors.json has no caddy entry, so this is the abap precedent — simple-icons' hex stands where the source of truth is silent. One more number, recorded because it is under the floor: the ring's wall is 1.07 px at this envelope (outer 12.80, counter 10.65) and the mark's runs are 0.84 px at the 25th percentile. That is the chrome situation — official detail kept at official proportions, because thickening the ring means shrinking Caddy's shed inside it.

flags.title: c3's gradient is flattened per letter rather than for the whole mark
flags.text: c3-lang.org draws the "C3" logotype as ONE path with a horizontal #2563EB → #7C3AED gradient across it, which means the C sits in the blue end and the 3 in the violet end. Flattening the whole mark to one stop is the letter of the chrome ruling and would throw away half of what the mark looks like, so it is flattened per subpath instead: the C takes offset 0, the 3 takes offset 1. No geometry moves and the two hexes are the brand's own. Letters: this is a faithful logotype from the brand's own file, so L3's typeset-letter ban does not reach it — the abap / al / typescript reading. Its sustained ink runs are 1.72 px at the 25th percentile and 2.00 at the median, thicker than abap's SAP letters which the A01 gate passed at 1.00–1.25 px.

flags.title: circom's bar takes the LIGHT end of its gradient, against the chrome default
flags.text: circom's symbol is achromatic — a white C-ring with a bar driven through it — and the bar is painted with a #C6C6C6 → #4E4E4E gradient. The offset 1 stop the chrome ruling would take measures 2.24:1 against #121314, which trips the 3.0:1 lift trigger; and lifting an ACHROMATIC ink lands it at L 88 = #E0E0E0, which is the white ring the bar exists to contrast with — the lift would erase the mark's only tonal difference. So the bar takes offset 0, #C6C6C6 at 10.89:1, and the mark stays two-tone. Recorded because it is the second flattening in this tranche that does not take offset 1, and both are for the same reason: the lift trigger and the gradient ends disagree.

flags.title: RULE 2 in practice — one object glyph and four brackets, the smallest collapse yet
flags.text: Five of the twenty-eight own no usable mark, which is 18% against A01 tranche 2's 37% — the D22 amendment is why, and this tranche is the first built entirely under it. chess gets an OBJECT glyph, a new one: no brand owns chess (.pgn is a 1994 community standard, .fen is from a newspaper column), so it takes a piece, and which piece was decided by measurement in proofs/chess-piece-study.png. Four take the bracket glyph, and only ONE of them is a mark that exists and cannot ship: capnp, whose logo is an eleven-letter Victorian wordmark published as a 635×356 PNG with no symbol anywhere in the project — and tracing a raster is the FIDELITY rule the amendment does not reach, which ends it before the legibility question is. The other three own no mark at all: brainfuck is a 1993 esolang with no project, cddl is IETF RFC 8610, and cbx is a BibLaTeX citation style. All four payloads are byte-identical to A01's thirteen and the slice check asserts that across the slice boundary.

flags.title: bosque, bruno, cairo, cangjie, casc, ceylon and chef ship from third-party vectors
flags.text: L2 asks for the brand's own vector first and the hunt is recorded rather than assumed. Six came up empty, each for a different reason (chef is a seventh and has its own flag: the vector chef.io serves is the Progress corporate mark). bosque: every file in microsoft/BosqueLanguage's resources/brand/ tree whose name ends in .svg is a PNG in an <image> wrapper — the Fluent icon is 248 KB of base64 at 4096 px, the combined lockup 697 KB. bruno: usebruno/bruno ships logo.png and no vector, and simple-icons' entry is a monochrome outline. cairo: starkware-libs/cairo, cairo-book and cairo-lang.org publish PNG only. cangjie: cangjie-lang.cn serves its logo from a CDN as a PNG. casc: CASC-Lang's only artwork is CASC-Vscode/icon.png. ceylon: the project is archived and its site tree holds ceylon-logo.png only. All six ship from a faithful vector of the same drawing — four from vscode-icons, one from gilbarbara/logos — which is the A01 antlr precedent, and every one was checked against the official raster before it was used.

flags.title: casc is a JVM language, not Blizzard's archive format
flags.text: Recorded because the acronym is genuinely ambiguous and the wrong reading would have put a game publisher's mark on a source file. "CASC" is best known as Blizzard's Content Addressable Storage Container, a binary game-data archive. The roster's casc is not that: it is CASC-Lang/CASC, a JVM language, and the evidence is vscode-icons' own icon request (issue #2688), which names the language, links its marketplace extension (ChAoS-UnItY.casc-lang) and attaches the aperture logo this icon is built from. The reduction: the mark sets "CA SC" in white across the aperture's black centre, and at the shipped fit each of those four letters lands in a 1.82×2.54 px box — strokes at a fraction of a pixel — so they are dropped; the black field goes with them, because the source leaves it unfilled (black measures 1.13:1 against #121314) and it paints nothing a reader can see. What ships is the eight-bladed aperture, which is what the mark is.

flags.title: cake and bower keep dark contour tones that the backdrop swallows
flags.text: Three marks in this tranche carry a tone under the 3.0:1 lift trigger, and none of them is lifted. The measurements: cake's #4A1700 outline at 1.25:1, bower's #543729 keyline at 1.73:1, bosque's two darkest back tiles at 2.43:1 and 2.93:1. In all three the tone is a CONTOUR or a SHADE inside a multi-colour drawing, not the mark's ink: it prints against the mark's own bright fills for most of its length, and lifting it to L 88 would put the palest colour of the icon on its outermost edge and invert the drawing's tonal order. The lift is opt-in per subject exactly so this can be declined, and the pilot's dotenv erratum is the same reading from the other side. What it costs at 16 px: all three read by their bright fills rather than by their outlines — the cake by its sponge and icing, the bird by its head and wing, the Bosque tiles by the front one. That is what these marks do on any dark ground.

flags.title: cuda wears NVIDIA's eye — the company-mark rider, used for the third time
flags.text: A .cu or .cuh is a CUDA C++ source. CUDA is NVIDIA's language, NVIDIA's toolkit and NVIDIA's trademark, and it has NO symbol of its own — NVIDIA brands it as a "CUDA" wordmark set beside the corporate eye. So the rider ratified at the A01 gate (a format created and owned by a company may wear that company's mark, safetensors → Hugging Face, bolt → Firebase) is what puts a mark on this file type at all, and this is its third use after safetensors and tranche 1's cds. The sourcing is the brand's own: nvidia.com serves the eye as a vector in its brochure assets (nvidia-logo-black.svg, an Illustrator export titled "NVIDIA_Logo_V"); the wordmark and the registered-trademark glyph are dropped. vscode-icons and Material both draw the same eye for cuda, which is corroboration and not the source. What to weigh: a .cu file now carries a company logo rather than a language mark, and NVIDIA's eye will read as "NVIDIA" rather than "CUDA" to anyone who knows it. The alternative is the bracket glyph, which says nothing at all.

flags.title: cssmap ships CSS's own letter plate, and its field measures 2.21:1
flags.text: A .css.map is a CSS source map, so CSS's mark applies, and CSS has had an official one since 2024: the rebeccapurple (#663399) rounded field with "CSS" knocked out of it, published CC0 at CSS-Next/logo.css and carried by simple-icons as css. Two things to check before agreeing. The field: #663399 measures 2.21:1 against #121314 — under the 3.0:1 lift trigger — so on the product backdrop the plate is dim and the white letters carry the mark. That is A01's aspx exactly (a #512BD4 field at 2.34:1, passed at the gate) and it is treated identically: official colours verbatim, no lift, because lifting a field to L 88 leaves white ink on near-white. The letters: the repository publishes THREE cuts and this icon takes css.small.svg, the brand's own small-size variant, whose letters run 1.10 / 1.25 / 1.40 px against the standard cut's 0.85 / 0.95 / 1.05 — over L5's official-forced floor where the standard cut is under it. The brand did the prettier rider's work itself; both are in proofs/A02-t2-study.png. One consequence: when a later slice reaches css — and it will, plus scss, less and postcss — the ids will want the same mark and will have to be declared a family across slices.

flags.title: codeql takes GitHub's geometry and the Marketplace icon's blue, not the file's gray
flags.text: GitHub publishes a mark for CodeQL itself — github/vscode-codeql ships media/logo.svg, a rounded-square frame with "QL" in it — so the company-mark rider is not needed here. What IS a judgement is the colour. That file paints the mark #24292F, GitHub's light-UI ink, which measures 1.27:1 against #121314: on the product backdrop it is not there, and the lift would put CodeQL's mark at L 88, a near-white GitHub does not print. The same directory holds media/VS-marketplace-CodeQL-icon.png, the product icon the Marketplace shows, and a colour census of it returns #1E7DFF on white — the same mark in the brand's full-colour form, at 4.81:1. So the geometry comes from the vector and the colour from the brand's own colour publication of the same mark, which is the npm/git/go source-of-truth rule and the move tranche 1 made for cakephp. vscode-icons independently draws this mark in the same blue. To overturn: rule that the file's own gray ships and it lifts to #DCE0E4 in one edit.

flags.title: confluence ships Atlassian's CURRENT tile mark, not the sails every icon set draws
flags.text: A .confluence file is Confluence wiki markup, so the product's own mark applies. The sourcing is unusual and worth recording: Atlassian publishes no downloadable SVG on its brand pages — the brand portal is a JavaScript application — but it publishes its logos AS CODE, in @atlaskit/logo (Apache-2.0, Atlassian Pty Ltd, its own design system package), where every product mark is an inline SVG string. Version 21.6.0's confluence/icon.js is the CURRENT mark: a #1868DB rounded tile with the two white sails on it. What that changes: vscode-icons, devicon and gilbarbara all draw the LEGACY mark — the standalone gradient-blue sails with no tile — which is what most people picture. Atlassian retired it; the same package still carries it under legacy-logos/. This icon follows the brand rather than the icon sets, which means a plate mark (R8 scores its glyph, like abap and aspx) rather than a free silhouette. To overturn: say the legacy sails ship and they do, from the same package.

flags.title: csproj joins A01's .NET family — five ids now look the same
flags.text: A .csproj is an MSBuild project file for a .NET project, and A01's fix round already ruled asp and aspx one family on Microsoft's own CC0 .NET logo, reduced by the prettier rider to the official dot and N at 2.5x. csproj is the same family and ships the same bytes. Branch (a) was checked and is not empty: vscode-icons draws a csproj icon — the VISUAL STUDIO ribbon with a green "C#" laid over it. It is declined because that is the IDE's corporate mark composed with a language monogram: Visual Studio does not own .csproj (MSBuild does, and dotnet build reads it without an IDE anywhere), and Microsoft publishes no csproj mark. What it costs in the tree: .asp, .aspx, .ascx, .asa and .csproj are now one picture. That is rule 1(b) working as written. To overturn: rule that the C# language mark may stand for its project file and csproj gets its own hunt.

flags.title: dal is A01's al-dal under a second id — the roster gives both the same extension
flags.text: Recorded because it looks like a duplicate and is one. The roster gives A02's dal the extension .dal AND the language id dal, and gives A01's al-dal the extension .dal — two concepts, one file type, which is the asp/aspx situation A01 already ruled on. What a .dal is comes from vscode-icons' own icon requests: #1159 asks for the AL icon "via language id al, dal", and #3125 describes .dal as "AL Language definition files ... reconstructed on the fly by the AL Language". So it is Microsoft's AL, one file type down, and it takes Microsoft's own AL mark — the same bytes as A01's al and al-dal and tranche 1's c-al. Branch (a) is empty twice over: vscode-icons' file_type_dal.svg (the one registered against the language id) is a BAR CHART with a rising arrow, a generic analytics metaphor, and its file_type_al_dal.svg is the AL monogram recoloured dusty red, which A01 already declined as the theme's own invention. In the tree four ids now carry Microsoft's AL lockup.

flags.title: clojurescript keeps a wordmark that does not resolve at 16 px
flags.text: The flag most likely to be argued with in this tranche. ClojureScript's mark is the "cljs" logotype inside a two-tone ring, and clojurescript.org publishes it as PNG only (images/cljs-logo-icon-256.png), so the geometry is vscode-icons' faithful vector — whose two hexes a colour census of the official PNG confirms. The numbers: at the open envelope (13.6×13.6, the widest the mass system allows and itself forced by L5) the mark's sustained ink runs are 0.50 / 0.70 / 0.95 px, and measured alone the four letters run 0.45 / 0.55 / 0.60 px — half of abap's SAP letters, which the A01 gate passed at 1.00–1.25. At 16 px they are a smudge. Why they stay: "cljs" IS the mark. Strip it and what is left is a bare ring, which says nothing about ClojureScript and would join four other rings in this slice alone (cue, cypress-spec, coconut, and tranche 1's chef) — the gestalt failure the pilot ruling names. Both builds are in proofs/A02-t2-study.png. To overturn: say the ring ships alone and it does, in one edit — or rule that ClojureScript may wear Clojure's own mark (the interlocking circles), which is the family reading and would need a clojure subject to be the base.

flags.title: dinophp's mark has a real vector and is declined on L8's byte cap and L5
flags.text: The first subject in the set where a BRAND-TIER vector is rejected by the format law rather than by legibility alone. A .bubble is a template for the Bubble engine of the DinoPHP framework, and DinoPHP publishes its red dinosaur at DinoPHP/vscode-bubble images/DinoPHP-icon.svg — seven paths, #E92744 and white, and the drawing Material traces. The two numbers: fitted at the compact envelope the icon is 6,461 bytes, 60% past L8's 4 KB hard cap (a fail, not the 2 KB advisory), and its sustained ink runs are 0.40 / 0.80 / 1.40 px — tranche 1's rejected Buck 2 deer (0.22 / 0.38 / 0.88) in the same territory. Why there is no reduction: every layer is a body part — head, neck, tail, two legs, eye — so nothing sub-pixel can be deleted; dropping one removes a limb. Opening the envelope to 13.6×13.6 moves the runs to 0.40 / 0.85 / 1.50 and the bytes to 6,507. All of it is rendered in proofs/A02-t2-collapse-study.png. To overturn: rule that the 4 KB cap may be raised for a full-colour animal, and the dinosaur ships as built.

flags.title: codekit collapses to the bracket glyph, and its own mark IS a bracket pair
flags.text: Written down because the irony is real and a reviewer should see it rather than discover it. CodeKit's mark is a pair of black angle brackets on an orange tile — the same object the set's generic-code glyph draws in gray. It is published as RASTER ONLY: codekitapp.com serves images/apple-touch-icon.png and images/favicon-32.png (its other SVGs are feature icons), and github.com/bdkjones/codekit is an issue tracker with no artwork in it. Tracing a raster is what L2 forbids on FIDELITY grounds — the one rule the D22 amendment does not reach. vscode-icons is not a way round it: its file draws the brackets on a BLACK DISC in inverted colours (its own commit message says "Convert PNG to SVG"), and that disc measures 1.13:1 against #121314, so what would arrive is two white brackets on nothing — which is the collapse glyph with extra steps. What the collapse costs, precisely: the tile and the orange, not the idea. To overturn: rule that an official tile may be re-drawn as a plate under traced bracket geometry, and codekit ships branded.

flags.title: coconut lifts BOTH of its inks — the first two-ink lift in the set
flags.text: Coconut's mark is a black ring around a lambda whose upper arm is a palm frond, and every ink in it is too dark for this backdrop: #000000 at 1.13:1 (the ring) and #7E3B1B at 2.24:1 (the palm), both under the 3.0:1 trigger. The lift is opt-in per subject and here it is taken TWICE, each ink going to L 88 with hue and saturation intact (#E0E0E0 and #F4D9CD). What that costs: the two inks now sit at the same lightness, so the mark is told apart by hue and shape rather than by tone — it arrives pale, where the official mark is black-and-brown on white. The alternatives, both rendered in proofs/A02-t2-study.png: dropping the invisible ring the way tranche 1's casc drops its black field (buys runs of 1.00 / 1.40 / 1.50 px and loses the mark's outer form), or shipping the official inks unlifted (a mark you cannot see). Sourcing note, also new: the vector is the BRAND's own potrace of its own logo — coconut-lang.org/safari-pinned-tab.svg, published for Safari pinned tabs — because evhub/coconut contains no image files at all. It is single-colour, which is why the frond's green (#076007) is lost: trunk and frond are one contour in it, and splitting them would be drawing.

flags.title: cypress-spec ships the brand's own DARK-MODE artwork
flags.text: A find worth recording because it is the first time a brand answered the lift question for us. cypress.io/favicon.svg carries a <style> block with a @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) section: on a dark ground Cypress repaints its "cy" white (from #1B1E2E, which measures 1.13:1 here and would otherwise have needed the lift) and swaps one arc's gradient from #58D09E → #1B1E2E to #58D09E → #FFFFFF. This icon ships that reading, so nothing about its colour is our invention. The four arcs flatten to the solid stop #58D09E they share, and the "y" is a <polygon> re-emitted as a path (the casc conversion). Two notes: the ring's wall is 1.05 px, under L5's official-forced floor, which is what makes the verdict marginal; and this is the SPEC id wearing the base Cypress mark, which is not a family declaration because no cypress subject exists in the pilot or an approved slice yet — when one does, the two will have to be declared one family, the same note tranche 1 leaves for bucklescript/rescript.

flags.title: dartlang-generated ships Dart's base mark, and the themes' recolours are declined
flags.text: .g.dart and .freezed.dart are the files build_runner writes beside a Dart source, so this is Dart's own file type. Rule 1 asks branch (a) first — an established NON-LETTER variant glyph in the source themes — and both themes have one: Material paints the Dart mark GRAY for generated files, vscode-icons paints it RED. Both are declined for the reason A01 declined al-dal's dusty red: a theme recolouring a brand's mark is the theme's invention, where the (recolour) branch is for brands that draw their own variants that way (TOTVS's advpl). So the base mark ships under this id, from Dart's own dart-lang/site-shared vector. Two consequences: a .g.dart and a .dart will look identical once a later slice ships dart — and at that point the two ids must be declared a family across slices, because nothing in the set can be the base today. What was dropped: the file's white gradient gloss and two highlight slivers that render under the mark's own dark face; both builds were compared pixel for pixel.

flags.title: cython paints the Python logo inside its C in the SET's python hexes
flags.text: Cython's own vector paints its two snakes with Python's own gradients (#306998 → #5A9FD4 and #FFD43B → #FFE873). Flattening them per the chrome ruling would put two different Python blues in one set for one logo, because the pilot already ships the identical mark — python — at #3776AB / #FFD43B, which is brand-colors.json's python entry and the source of truth. So the snakes take the set's python hexes and the "C", which is Cython's own and not Python's, keeps the file's #646464. One number worth seeing: that #646464 measures 3.14:1 against #121314 — over the 3.0:1 lift trigger by four hundredths. It is not lifted, and how close that is is recorded rather than hidden. To overturn: rule that the artwork's own stops win over the set's hex and the snakes go to #306998, a blue that measures 3.19:1.

flags.title: devenv, dartlang-generated and coala keep dark tones the backdrop swallows
flags.text: Four marks in this tranche carry a tone under the 3.0:1 lift trigger and none of them is lifted. The measurements: devenv's #425C82 blue squares at 2.73:1, dartlang-generated's #01579B shadow faces at 2.51:1, coala's #2C3E50 nose at 1.69:1 and #37495E eye at 2.02:1, and cssmap's #663399 field at 2.21:1. Each declines the lift for a reason the set has already ruled on: coala's two print on the koala's own field (the pilot's dotenv erratum — ink on the mark's own field is never lifted); dart's is the shaded side of a two-tone mark whose light faces measure 9.35:1 and 8.07:1, so lifting it would invert the drawing's tonal order (tranche 1's bosque reading); devenv's is one half of a deliberately two-tone mark whose other half is #FBFBFB, so lifting it would make all eight squares near-white and delete the drawing; and cssmap's is A01's aspx case, where lifting the field leaves white letters on near-white. What it costs at 16 px: devenv reads white-first with the blue squares as shadow, dart reads as a light mark with a dark fold, and cssmap reads as white letters with a violet ground. That is what these marks do on any dark ground.

flags.title: FIVE subjects take the lift — the largest group in the set so far
flags.text: The contrast-derived trigger the A01 fix round ruled in (backdrop-meeting ink under 3.0:1 against #121314 lifts to L 88, hue and saturation intact) fires for five of this tranche's twenty branded subjects, where the whole set had three callers before it. The reason is a category rather than an accident: these are MONOCHROME marks drawn for light pages. The numbers: crystal #000000 at 1.13:1 (and brand-colors.json records that black itself), coffeescript #2F2625 at 1.26:1, cue #232A68 at 1.42:1, dhall #484848 at 2.03:1, coconut #000000 and #7E3B1B at 1.13:1 and 2.24:1. Two of them are worth a second look: cue's navy is the site's own $c-blue, and the brand solves the same problem differently — its header prints the mark on a white disc rather than lightening it; and coffeescript and crystal are inside L6's achromatic exemption (S 11.7 and S 0), so their lift moves lightness only. If the lift is wrong for any of them the alternative is a white disc behind the mark, which is a container this style does not have, or an icon you cannot see.

flags.title: coala drops 43 KB of the official drawing's own line art
flags.text: coala's logo file is a 2015 Inkscape drawing and the honest description of it is a mess: it carries the artwork TWICE (once painted with xlink-chained gradients that hold no stops, once in flat fills), plus TWO black line-art layers of 17,280 and 26,396 characters, plus a 0.65-opacity PNG tracing underlay in an <image> tag. What ships is the FLAT copy — green disc, koala head, cheek shade, nose, mouth, two eyes — at 1.7 KB. The line art is dropped for bruno's two reasons at once: 43,676 characters is ten times L8's 4 KB hard cap on its own, and black measures 1.13:1 against #121314, so it paints nothing a reader can see. Why this is not editorconfig's failure: the pilot rejected flattening a mark that is REALLY a line drawing into a silhouette; coala's drawing has flat colour layers of its own and they are what ships — the koala keeps its shape, its shading and its face. The <image> underlay is stripped on fetch (L8 bans it, and a tracing underlay is not part of the drawing), which is the only edit made to any fetched file in this tranche.

flags.title: cocos drops its frame and its wordmark — the mascot alone fills the envelope
flags.text: Cocos publishes no vector (cocos.com serves CDN rasters; cocos/cocos-engine keeps editor/dashboard/logo.png), so the geometry is simple-icons' faithful vector of the mascot mark — the flame-headed character in a square frame with "COCOS" beneath it. Eighteen subpaths, and eleven of them go. The letters: each is 2.4–2.9×3.7 units on a 24-unit canvas, about 1.5 px tall at the fit with strokes a fraction of that. The frame: its rule is 0.40 px, and holding it in the fit costs the mascot the envelope — with the frame the whole mark runs 0.15 / 0.40 / 0.45 px, without it 0.40 / 0.95 / 1.55. That is tranche 1's casc reduction on the same reasoning (drop the field the reader cannot see, let the symbol fill the box). What is kept: the head, its outline and the two eyes; the six sub-pixel face details go. Both builds are in proofs/A02-t2-study.png.

flags.title: RULE 2 in practice — one reused object glyph and seven brackets, three of them marks that exist
flags.text: Eight of the twenty-eight own no usable mark — 29%, against tranche 1's 18% and A01 tranche 2's 37%. command takes an OBJECT glyph and it is A01's, not a new one: a .command file is a shell script Finder runs in Terminal, which is the object .bat and .awk name, so it ships geom.terminalGlyph byte for byte across the slice boundary (Material draws the ⌘ key symbol, which reads the name rather than the file). Seven take the bracket glyph, and THREE of those are concepts whose mark exists: codekit and denizenscript publish theirs as raster only, which L2's fidelity rule ends, and dinophp publishes a real vector that fails L8's byte cap and L5 together (its own flag). The other four own no mark at all: cobol is a 1959 ISO standard (vscode-icons draws a triceratops, a joke about its age), coloredpetrinets is a formalism plus ISO/IEC 15909-2, context is ConTeXt — whose only mark is a logotype living in a FONT, tranche 1's cbx ruling exactly — and controller is an MVC file-naming convention. All seven payloads are byte-identical to A01's thirteen and tranche 1's four, and the slice check asserts that across the slice boundary.

flags.title: the ambiguous names, and what the roster made them
flags.text: Recorded because a wrong reading here would have put a real brand's mark on the wrong file type, and each of these was checked rather than assumed. command: .command with no language id is the macOS shell script Terminal runs on a double-click — not the ⌘ key, which is what Material draws. controller: .controller.js/.ts, icon-pack only, is the MVC controller layer of an Angular/Ngrx/Qwik app — a naming convention with no owner. context: .ctx with language id context is ConTeXt, the TeX macro package; Material added its icon in the "TeX/LaTeX related files" PR #3042, which is the corroboration. devenv: devenv.nix / devenv.lock / devenv.yaml is devenv.sh, the Nix developer-environment tool — NOT Visual Studio's devenv.exe. cssmap: .css.map is a CSS source map, so CSS's mark applies. cue: .cue with language id cue is the CUE configuration language, not a CD cue sheet. cocos: .prefab / .scene are Cocos Creator's scene files, so the engine's mark applies rather than a generic scene metaphor.

flags.title: conan drops the JFrog frog its own lockup carries
flags.text: The mirror of tranche 1's chef flag, and it comes out the same way. Conan's own brand file — conan-io/conan .github/conan2-logo-for-dark.svg — is a lockup: the isometric Conan cube on the left, a divider rule, then the "CONAN 2.0 / C/C++ Package Manager" wordmark and the green JFROG FROG. JFrog owns Conan, and the company-mark rider covers a company standing in for a format IT owns — but Conan HAS its own mark, so the frog would be a parent company's symbol standing in for a product that does not need it, which is the Progress/Chef situation exactly. The cube ships; the frog, the rule and the wordmark are dropped. The flattening: the cube's two gradient faces take their offset-1 stop #21AFFF (7.65:1); the offset-0 stop #0086FD measures 5.16:1 and either would read, so the chrome default stands.

flags.title: drools — Drools' own mark was built, rendered and declined on L5
flags.text: The flag to argue with first. A .drl is a Drools rule file and Drools HAS a mark — the line-drawn face in profile, red contour, blue eye-line, orange tongue, purple brow — carried as a vector by gilbarbara/logos. It was fetched, built at the tall envelope and rasterised at a true 16 px, and it is declined on measurements rather than on taste. The numbers: its sustained ink runs are 0.50 / 0.55 / 0.55 / 0.75 px at the 5th, 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles, with 9.8% of the canvas inked — thinner at the median than the Buck 2 deer tranche 1 rejected (0.22 / 0.38 / 0.88). The eye-line is 0.94 px wide, the brow 2.11 × 0.75 px, and what arrives at 16 px is a red loop with three coloured specks in it (proofs/A02-t3-study.png). The prettier rider does not reach it: the rider reduces a mark's ELEMENT COUNT and thickens what is left, and here every element is a hairline, so thickening means redrawing the brand's own line weights end to end. The other mark this hunt found is not Drools': drools.org now serves the Apache KIE umbrella logo (its file is literally captioned "KIE Logo"), which is the mirror of the company-mark rider and the case tranche 1 declined for chef. To overturn: either rule that the KIE mark may stand for a .drl — one fetch, and it lands — or rule that a hairline mark may ship thickened, which reopens the deer and the dinosaur with it.

flags.title: doctex / doctex-installer / dtx — the LaTeX Project's kingfisher, reduced to its silhouette
flags.rule: L2 / L5 / prettier rider / working rule 1
flags.text: Three roster ids, one file family, one mark — and a reduction big enough to be worth arguing with. A .dtx is a literate LaTeX source, an .ins the docstrip installer that unpacks it, and the language id doctex names the same format, so all three take one mark and the family is declared. Which mark: LaTeX's recognisable mark is the "LaTeX" LOGOTYPE set in its own font, which R1 cannot ship (the ConTeXt case tranche 2 ruled on) — but the LaTeX PROJECT publishes real artwork at latex3/branding, the teal kingfisher that heads latex-project.org, and the company-mark rider ratified at the A01 gate says a format created and owned by a company may wear that company's mark. Same rider as cds/SAP one tranche back. The reduction, and both halves of it are forced: the bird is drawn with twenty-two WHITE FEATHER LINES over it, which measure 0.23–2.05 px at this envelope with eighteen of them under a pixel — and keeping them makes the icon 6,984 bytes against L8's 4 KB hard cap. Dropped, the icon is 1,739 bytes and the bird's own silhouette, jagged wing edge and all. Both builds are in proofs/A02-t3-study.png. Why this is not the editorconfig failure: that mascot's spectacles and features WERE the mark, so flattening destroyed it; these lines are feather texture inside a silhouette that still reads as a kingfisher at 16 px. To overturn: rule that an organisation's bird may not stand for a macro file and all three join the brackets — or that the flattening loses too much, which is the same outcome.

flags.title: edge — the only SVG the brand publishes is a solid square
flags.text: Worth reading because the hunt result sounds like a mistake and is not. An .edge is an Edge template (edgejs.dev, the engine AdonisJS ships — not Microsoft's browser, and Material's own icon for the id is "@", Edge's tag sigil). Its icon is a mint tile with a white frame and three white waves, and it is published as apple-touch-icon.png plus the android-chrome and favicon PNGs. The site's public/ tree does contain one SVG — safari-pinned-tab.svg — and that file is a potrace of a solid square: a single path whose only geometry is the 512 × 512 canvas outline. It is fetched and kept as sources-svg/edge-official-pinned.svg and rendered in proofs/A02-t3-study.png in the brand's own sampled #4CBBA5, so the claim can be checked rather than believed. vscode-icons draws a red serif "E" — a monogram in a colour the brand does not print. To overturn: rule that the PNG may be traced and the tile-and-waves ships.

flags.title: dune — the brand's only image is a painting of a sand dune, and it ships
flags.text: The one call in this tranche that goes the other way, so it should be the easiest to disagree with. dune, dune-project and dune-workspace are the OCaml build system's files, and Dune publishes no mark at all: its only brand image is assets/imgs/dune_favicon.png, a PAINTED sand dune with a lit crest and a shadowed face, and ocaml/dune's repository carries no logo. A painted illustration has no vector geometry to recover, so a trace of it is an interpretation rather than a recovery — which is the argument for collapsing it. What ships instead is vscode-icons' four-layer flat reading of that same picture, and what justifies it is that BOTH source themes read the picture the same way (Material draws the same dune as an orange silhouette), which is the agreement L2's faithful-vector tier asks for. It renders well — runs 7.15 / 10.50 / 12.00 px, the thickest mark in the tranche. To overturn: rule that a picture is not a mark and dune joins the brackets, which is a one-line change.

flags.title: eex and erb wear Elixir's and Ruby's own marks — and the family is FUTURE work
flags.text: Two kin concepts with no base in the set yet, handled the way tranche 2 handled generated Dart. An .eex is an Embedded Elixir template and an .erb an Embedded Ruby one, so the marks that apply are Elixir's drop and Ruby's gem — and both brands publish them (elixir-lang.github.com's src/assets/icons/logo-elixir-light.svg, ruby-lang.org's images/header-ruby-logo.svg). Rule 1's branch (a) was checked for both: vscode-icons draws the Elixir drop itself for eex, and for erb it draws the gem as a dark-red OUTLINE — a recolour and a hollowing, which is the theme's own invention rather than a variant the brand draws (A01's al-dal reading). So both ship the base mark under their own id. No family is declared, because there is no elixir and no ruby subject in the pilot or in an approved slice to be byte-identical TO. What the next slice inherits: when elixir and ruby arrive, each has to be declared one family with its template id here — otherwise the twin audit will see two identical marks and fail them as undeclared twins, which is exactly what happened to al and dal inside this slice.

flags.title: falcon — which Falcon, and an extension that matches none of them
flags.text: A name call, made from the artwork rather than from the roster, because the roster here is thin: it gives this concept the extension .falcon and the language id falcon, both from vscode-icons' icon pack, and no shipping Falcon writes .falcon files — the Python web framework's are .py, Falcon P/L's are .fal, and the marketplace's "Falcon Language" extension (vopple) registers .fl, .fle and .fles. What decides it is the mark vscode-icons draws for the id: a bird in flight, in oranges. The only Falcon that publishes a bird is the Python web framework, whose own falconframework.org/assets/logo.svg is the orange falcon with its wings spread and its talons down, and whose brand hex simple-icons records as #F0AD4E — the colour the drawing paints. So the framework's own vector ships. Two things to know: at 16 px it reads as "an orange bird" rather than as a falcon (runs 0.25 / 0.65 / 1.45 px), and at 4,070 bytes it is the largest icon in the slice, 26 bytes under L8's 4 KB hard cap. To overturn: rule that the id means Falcon P/L and it becomes a fresh hunt (that brand's mark is a stylised falcon head, published as raster).

flags.title: elm — the geometry is the brand's vector, the COLOURS are sampled from its raster
flags.text: A first for this set, so it is flagged rather than buried in a simplification log. Elm publishes its tangram as a vector — seven <polygon> pieces in elm/foundation.elm-lang.org — but that file is the REVERSED cut: every piece is fill="white". The four-colour original sits beside it as assets/logo.png, a raster. Three third-party traces exist and all three disagree about the hexes (vscode-icons #5FB4CB/#EEA400/#596277/#8CD636, devicon #60B5CC/#EFA500/#34495E/#8DD737, Material its own palette). So the geometry comes from the brand's vector and each polygon's CENTROID was projected into the brand's own PNG and the pixel under it read: #60B5CC, #5A6378, #60B5CC, #7FD13B, #7FD13B, #F0AD00, #F0AD00 in document order, off a colour box that measures exactly 300 × 300 px. Why this is not the raster trace L2 bans: no geometry comes from the picture — the mark's shapes are the brand's own vector coordinates, and the raster answers one question the vector cannot ("what colour is this piece?"). To overturn: rule that a trace's palette is preferable to sampling and one of the three gets picked instead.

flags.title: duckdb / emacs / ember — three round marks, and the look-alike lane
flags.text: The tranche's twin-audit finding, declared rather than hidden. Three of its marks are round because their brands draw them round: DuckDB's duck head, GNU Emacs's sphere, Ember's disc. emacs and ember are PLATE marks — an official field carrying a glyph — so the audit scores them against each other glyph to glyph (a white swirl against a white "e") and they pass. duckdb is not a plate: its yellow disc is the duck's HEAD and the dark shapes are its eye and beak, and declaring it a field to move it into that lane would be a misdeclaration made to satisfy a gate. Scored honestly, silhouette against silhouette, duckdb vs emacs is 0.940 and duckdb vs ember 0.986 on the 0.72 bar. Both pairs are therefore DECLARED look-alikes (the antlr / chrome instrument, opened at the A01 fix round): the audit prints their live scores every run and the separator is colour and interior — 173.6 degrees of hue against Emacs, 49.2 degrees and 27.1 points of saturation against Ember. To overturn: Ember's own brand kit publishes the same "e" as a ROUNDED SQUARE and as a plain square, both equally official, so ruling "no two full discs" costs one fetch and settles that pair; the emacs pair has no non-round cut on either side and would have to be ruled on as it stands.

flags.title: ejs — the brand's own mark ships under L5's floor
flags.text: EJS publishes its own vector (mde/ejs-site ejs.svg) and it ships whole, which means shipping under the floor: the crimson "eJS" letterforms measure 0.85 px at the 25th percentile and 1.00 at the median at the wide envelope, against L5's 1.2 px official-forced minimum. At 16 px the olive swoosh reads and the letters do not; at 22 the J and the S separate. The reason it ships anyway is that there is no thicker EJS to ship — these are the brand's own proportions, the prettier rider has no element count to reduce here, and tranche 2 shipped Cypress's 0.95 px ring on the same reading. To overturn: rule that a mark under the floor collapses and ejs joins the brackets.

flags.title: elastic — the brand hex paints nothing, and the mark's bar is theme-negative
flags.text: Two small things worth knowing before agreeing. The bar: Elastic's own component ships the Elasticsearch mark with its middle bar painted by the class euiIcon__fillNegative — black on a light ground, WHITE on a dark one. This set's ground is #121314, so the bar is white: that is the brand's own rule applied, not a colour we chose, and it is the same move tranche 2 made with Cypress's dark-mode favicon rules. The hex: the worklist and brand-colors.json both record elastic as #005571, and it stays the recorded primary even though no layer paints it — the mark is yellow, teal and white. #005571 measures 2.25:1 against the backdrop, which is exactly why Elastic does not use it in the icon either. The npm / git / dart precedent covers this (brand-colors wins the primary, the artwork's fills win the layers), and the folder pass is where it would actually paint something.

flags.title: dlang — the brand's banner is cropped, on the file's own instruction
flags.text: D's own images/dlogo.svg is a 481 × 89 STRIP — a width="100%" red rect with the white D and its two moons sitting in the right third — and its first comment line reads "This version is meant to be centered and cropped left/right as needed". So it is cropped: to the mark plus the banner's own top margin (10.44 units) on each side, which lands at 117.99 × 89, aspect 1.326 against the wide envelope's 1.353. The vertical extent is the banner's, untouched, and nothing else moves. It is flagged because a crop is still a choice: a different rule (crop to a square, crop tight to the mark) would give a different plate. To overturn: name the crop and it is one constant.

flags.title: docz — the mark's line art is dropped, and it costs the ruled lines
flags.text: Docz's mark is a cream scroll with dark line art and a quill, published as a 1836 × 444 PNG on a CDN (docz.site itself is a parked domain now, serving a placeholder whose icon is an Arial "?" in a magnifier). vscode-icons' vector is that drawing layer for layer, and one of its five layers — the line art — is 3,972 characters, which on its own is more than L8's 4 KB hard cap allows a finished icon. It is also unfilled in the source, so it paints black: 1.13:1 against the backdrop. Dropped, on tranche 1's bruno reading. What it costs: the scroll's ruled lines and the quill's contour, so at 16 px the icon reads as "a document with a pen" rather than as Docz's scroll. To overturn: rule that the line art matters more than the cap and the layer has to be simplified subpath by subpath to fit — a real piece of work, but a possible one.

flags.title: the collapse rate — ten of twenty-eight, and why this stretch of the alphabet
flags.text: Worth stating at slice level rather than leaving to arithmetic: this tranche collapses nine concepts to the bracket glyph and one to a new object glyph — 36%, against tranche 1's 18% and tranche 2's 29%. It is not a change of standard. Six of the nine are concepts whose mark EXISTS and could not ship, each for its own recorded reason (drools on L5; doxyfile because the mark is a word; dotjs, duc, dylan and edge because the mark is raster only) — and the remaining three own no mark at all (docpad, a DTD has no owner to draw one, and dustjs). What clusters here is the long tail's dead projects (DocPad 2018, Dust 2019, ENSIME 2018, Open Dylan) and its file-format NOUNS — a Doxyfile, a DTD, a .dtx — which is what the D-and-E stretch of an extension roster is made of. If the rate looks wrong, the flags above are where to push: five of them are single rulings that would each move one to three ids back out of the collapse.

flags.title: THE RULING — a mark whose FIELD cannot clear the backdrop may ship the brand's own FRAME
flags.rule: guide §5 lift/plate erratum, amended / L5 contrast duty
flags.text: Recorded first because it is a law and not a subject. Flag 1 declined Adobe's ColdFusion plate on a measurement — its #002258 field is 1.21:1 against #121314, so at 16 px the plate is not there and two pale letters are left floating. Sebastian overturned it with a directive: "In those cases you can use a background in a frame with their corners rounded (like in previous iterations)", and, asked which frame, picked the brand's own — "Adobe's own framed icon — fetch Adobe's actual ColdFusion product icon: bright rounded frame + dark field + Cf letters, colors verbatim." What that binds, set-wide: where a brand publishes a FRAMED construction, a mark whose own field cannot clear the backdrop may ship it. The frame carries the silhouette; the dark field inside it is then mark-interior ink, which the §5 erratum already says is never lifted (dotenv's black on its yellow field is the same reading). So the trigger for a dark plate is no longer "lift it or drop it" — it is "does the brand draw a frame?" What it does NOT change: the frame has to be the BRAND's, derived from the brand's own artwork like any other geometry (L2), and it still has to clear L5 at 16 px — an invented keyline, or one too thin to see, is not a construction, it is a decoration. Scale: three subjects in this slice. cf, cfc and cfm are the only ones the trigger reaches; every other plate in A02 already clears the backdrop on its own field.

flags.title: cf / cfc / cfm — Adobe's framed ColdFusion icon, and the one number the rider moved
flags.rule: L2 sourcing (ruled) / L8 / L5 prettier rider
flags.text: Provenance first, because the frame is Adobe's and not ours. Adobe publishes the ColdFusion mark twice and this build reads both, both fetched and both in the provenance pane. (1) coldfusion-official.svg, the 2021 logo, "Outline no shadow": a 56×54 #002258 rounded rect at rx/ry 9.9138 under a #7BADFF "Cf" in two paths — the plate, the corner radius, the letters and every colour. (2) coldfusion-framed-official.svg, Adobe's OWN framed ColdFusion product icon, fetched from adobe.com's product-icon directory and still carrying Adobe's internal filename cf_builder_2016_appicon.svg in its id: 256×249.6, a #CADBFE ring inset 10.7 around a #000F34 field. The frame constant, measured on four Adobe files rather than guessed: 10.7/256 = 4.18% here, and exactly 10/240 = w/24 on FrameMaker and RoboHelp, the two siblings Adobe serves from the same directory in the same generation, and on Adobe's rounded framed cut as well. The corners. Adobe's framed ColdFusion is SQUARE-cornered and the ruling asked for rounded, so the rounding comes from Adobe too: photoshop-ipad-official.svg is a 240×234 outer rect at r 42.5 around a 220×214 field at r 36.3, and 42.5/240 = 0.17708 is ColdFusion's own plate radius (9.9138/56 = 0.17703) to five decimals — the same rounded rectangle at two scales. So the outer radius is ColdFusion's own and the ONLY number borrowed from a sibling is the inner ratio, 36.3/42.5 = 0.8541. The one thing that had to change, and it is the flag to argue with. Adobe's w/24 frame is 2.33 units on the 56-wide plate, which is 0.53 px at the shipped fit — five times under L5's 1.2 px official-forced floor, and rendered in proofs/coldfusion-frame-study.png it is a halo, not a frame. The prettier rider thickens the one element that carries the silhouette, and it is thickened inside Adobe's own way of specifying it: the frame stays a fraction of the plate width and the denominator moves 24 → 10, giving 5.6 units = 1.28 px. w/11 was measured first and lands at 1.16 px, under the floor, so w/10 is the SMALLEST legal departure from Adobe's proportion rather than a weight somebody liked. L8: the frame is a filled RING, never a stroke — an outer contour with an inner one wound against it, punched by plain nonzero fill, which is how Adobe draws it too (it declares fill-rule:evenodd; this set emits none, so the winding does the work). A01's vsix flag records what happens when two subpaths are wound the same way and the counter never opens; that was checked for here. What it costs at 16 px: the frame reads and the letters are marginal — the "Cf" is 7.10×6.18 px at sustained ink runs of 0.97 / 1.06 / 1.19 px, so it arrives as an open arc beside a crossed stem rather than as crisp letterforms. That is Adobe's own drawing at this size, and thickening it would be redrawing a brand's letterforms, which L2 hard-rejects. To overturn: say the frame should be heavier and the denominator moves again — the study renders w/24, w/11 and w/10 side by side so the trade is visible rather than argued.

bower.title: Bower

source.name: Bower (brand's own SVG)
source.license: MIT (bower/bower.github.io)

The mark's sustained ink runs are 2.28 px at the 25th percentile and 4.38 at the median

the #543729 outline measures 1.73:1 against #121314 and is NOT lifted: it is the mark's own contour line, it prints against the head's orange for most of its length, and raising it to L 88 would draw Bower's bird with a white keyline. What it costs on the dark backdrop is that the bird reads by its five bright fills rather than by its outline, which is what the mark does on any dark ground

The green wing arrives as one wedge rather than as feathers and the gray beak is a 2.4 px speck, and the #543729 keyline is invisible on the backdrop by construction — so the bird reads by its five bright fills, which is what the mark does on any dark ground

source.name: none used — neutral glyph vocabulary (category: code)
source.note: Brainfuck is a 1993 esolang with no owner, no project site and no mark; nothing to hunt. Material draws a brain, which is a pun on the name rather than a mark, and vscode-icons draws nothing. The generic-code category glyph, shared byte for byte with A01's thirteen

proof_16px.note: the bracket pair, 2.2 px stems, byte-identical to A01's thirteen — this is A01's own verdict re-read at slice scale

source.name: Bruno (faithful vector — vscode-icons)
source.license: MIT (vscode-icons/vscode-icons); the Bruno artwork itself is MIT under usebruno/bruno. Recorded and NOT gating

It measures 1.13:1 against #121314, so on the product backdrop it paints nothing a reader can see; what it costs is that Bruno's head keeps its full outer contour instead of being trimmed by an invisible line. Both builds are in proofs/A02-t1-study.png

the eyes, the nose and the muzzle line are KEPT black: they print on the mark's own golden field, where the pilot's dotenv erratum says ink is never lifted, and they are what makes the shape a dog rather than a blob

buckbuild.title: Buck (Meta)

source.name: Buck (faithful vector — vscode-icons)
source.license: MIT (vscode-icons/vscode-icons); the Buck artwork is Apache-2.0 / MIT under facebook/buck. Recorded and NOT gating
source.note: 32x32, two #4A69A5 paths: the antler monogram and the arrowhead inside it. Buck 1 publishes this mark as docs/static/logo.png, a 300x150 raster, so the vector is a faithful trace of it (Material traces the same drawing in its own palette). BUCK 2 — the current generation, which reads the same .buckconfig — publishes its own vector at facebook/buck2 website/static/img/logo.svg, a leaping deer in an #AF4F39 -> #F69635 gradient; it is fetched to sources-svg/buck-official.svg, it wins the fidelity chain, and it loses to L5 (see the flag). Fetched to sources-svg/buck-vsicons.svg

simplifications: THE BRAND TIER WAS SOURCED AND DECLINED ON L5. Buck 2's own vector was fetched, fitted at two envelopes and measured: the deer's sustained ink runs are 0.22 px at the 5th percentile, 0.38 at the 25th and 0.88 at the MEDIAN — jar's numbers, which A01 rejected on L5 alone — and opening the envelope to 13.6 x 14.4 only moves them to 0.25 / 0.41 / 0.94. Buck 1's antler monogram runs 0.50 / 0.97 / 1.25 px at the same three percentiles, two to three times the deer at every one of them. Both renders are in proofs/A02-t1-study.png

NOT reduced, and the honest limit is recorded rather than dressed up: the monogram is a LINE DRAWING and its runs sit at 1.25 px at the median, under L5's 1.5 px floor and at the 1.2 px official-forced one. What saves it at 16 px is that every stroke is axis-aligned or at 45 degrees, so it lands on pixel edges instead of straddling them — the 16 px proof is where to check that, and it holds

colour is the trace's own #4A69A5, which is Buck's blue as its raster prints it (3.41:1 against #121314, clear of the lift trigger). brand-colors.json has no buck entry and simple-icons has none either, so there is nothing to reconcile it against

proof_16px.note: the antler monogram arrives whole — five tines, the muzzle line and the arrowhead all separate — and it is unmistakably a stag's head. Marginal because the strokes run 1.25 px at the median, under L5's floor: what saves them is that they are axis-aligned or at 45 degrees and land on pixel edges. The current generation's own vector, the deer, runs 0.88 px at the median and is an orange hook at this size — flagged

lookalike_lane.ruling: Sebastian, 2026-09-03 — "I like the icons that are actually the real Icon." Flag 18 offered exactly this as its second option: relax R8 for DECLARED pairs rather than take a real mark off a real brand.
lookalike_lane.why: ANTLR's mark is an orange-red disc with a white "A" and Chrome's is a red-yellow-green disc with a blue centre. They score R8 form 0.798 on a 0.72 bar (area IoU 0.969: two discs of the same diameter are one silhouette) and their dominant reds are 3.4 degrees of hue apart. Both are the brands' own artwork, neither can be refitted out of the collision — the envelope law has no room to shrink one disc by a quarter — and the alternative is a gray glyph on one of them. Rendered side by side at a true 16 / 22 / 32 px in proofs/antlr-chrome-study.png.

lookalike_lane.ruling: PROPOSED at the A02 gate — both marks are round by their own brands' drawing and are separated by colour and interior: 173.6 degrees of hue (#FFF100 against #211F46) and 30.2 points of lightness, with a dark eye and beak on one and a white swirl on the other

Form 0.940 on the 0.72 silhouette bar

lookalike_lane.ruling: PROPOSED at the A02 gate — separated by colour and interior: 49.2 degrees of hue (#FFF100 against #E04E39) with 27.1 points of saturation, a dark eye and beak on one and a white "e" knocked out of the other
lookalike_lane.why: Ember's brand kit publishes the same "e" as a circle, a rounded square and a plain square, and the circle is the cut the project uses as its own avatar and favicon — so unlike the emacs pair there IS a non-round official alternative here, and the flag names it as the overturn. Form 0.986 on the 0.72 silhouette bar, the highest in the slice

twin_audit.note: CROSS-SET: the pilot's 20 subjects, every subject the approved slice A01 shipped, and every subject this slice built are scored in one pool. THREE lanes are exempt from R8 and reported rather than failed, because in all three the identity is declared and deliberate — FAMILY (working rule 1), NEUTRAL COLLAPSE (working rule 2) and LOOK-ALIKE (opened by the A01 fix round, 2026-09-03: two brands whose real marks genuinely resemble each other may both keep them, and the pair is reported with its live scores every run). An undeclared pair scoring the same still fails. PLATE marks are scored glyph-to-glyph against m11's BADGE bar of 0.92.
